method: Direct model-authored translation from full English context. No external MT, translation tool, Google Translate or external LLM API used. Dictionary/native-language sources were consulted only for feasibility and terminology, not whole-message translation.

declined.name: Tibetan
declined.reason: Dictionary resources and scientific terminology are available, but I cannot reliably compose the causal, conditional and technical clauses required here in contemporary Tibetan; isolated terminology does not resolve that grammar gap.

declined.name: Dzongkha
declined.reason: The DDC computer glossary is identifiable, but the PDF fetch timed out. More fundamentally I cannot confidently author Dzongkha clause structure; Tibetan wording would not be an acceptable substitute.

declined.name: Dhivehi
declined.reason: The official Radheef dictionary is available as an app/web interface; it does not give me sufficient command of Dhivehi morphology and full technical clauses to guarantee the required meanings.

declined.name: Konkani
declined.reason: Bharatavani supplies dictionaries and administrative terminology. I cannot consistently produce distinctly Konkani full clauses instead of allowing Marathi/Hindi grammar to intrude; Goa official coverage specifically needs Devanagari.

declined.name: Kashmiri
declined.reason: Previously confirmed grammar and orthography gap persists; government dictionary resources do not make reliable sentence authorship possible for me.

declined.name: Santali
declined.reason: Prior examination of published Santali UI terminology supplied some nouns but did not establish enough Santali morphology and syntax for these messages. Do not substitute Bengali/Hindi or transliterate them.

declined.name: Zhuang
declined.reason: Prior published Zhuang UI terminology helped identify basic error vocabulary; I cannot compose the complete technical explanations in Standard Zhuang reliably.

declined.name: Pangasinan
declined.reason: The Benton dictionary is available, but I cannot confidently compose Pangasinan voice, aspect and conditional clauses for this material without substituting Ilocano/Tagalog patterns.

declined.name: Maguindanaon
declined.reason: SIL wordlists and a grammatical bibliography are available; my knowledge of Maguindanaon verbal inflection and clause structure is insufficient for all required source distinctions.

declined.name: Tausug
declined.reason: The SIL Tausug dictionary includes grammar notes, but lexical lookup does not overcome my inability to author the full request/permission/timeout clauses in defensible Tausug.

declined.name: Chamorro
declined.reason: A revised official dictionary and finder list exist. I cannot reliably supply Chamorro verbal affixes and clause grammar; the finder-list preface explicitly explains why English-word substitution is insufficient.

declined.name: Gilbertese (Kiribati)
declined.reason: A community dictionary supplies grammar guidance, but I cannot author the necessary aspect, negation and conditional constructions reliably in Kiribati.

declined.name: Marshallese
declined.reason: Dictionary examples are available, but my command of Marshallese agreement, particles and diacritic-bearing spelling is insufficient for defensible full technical messages.

declined.name: Nauruan
declined.reason: The historical Delaporte dictionary was identified but could not be fetched. I lack Nauruan sentence competence and cannot resolve modern technical phrasing from an old wordlist.

declined.name: Niuean
declined.reason: Government orthography guidance identifies dictionaries and grammatical resources; I still cannot compose reliable Niuean clauses. Tongan wording with changed spellings is not sufficient.

declined.name: Tahitian
declined.reason: Government resources point to the Fare Vānaʻa dictionary, whose site fetch failed. I cannot reliably distinguish Tahitian clause grammar and modern technical usage from related Polynesian languages. Official-status scope also needs separate treatment.

declined.name: Hiri Motu
declined.reason: Published grammar/dictionary research exists, but I do not have usable command of Hiri Motu sentence structure. Neither Tok Pisin nor ordinary Motu is a substitute.

declined.name: Palauan
declined.reason: The Palau Language Commission-associated dictionary has rich examples. I still lack reliable Palauan verb morphology and clause-level authorship for these technical messages.

declined.name: Tokelauan
declined.reason: The community-hosted government dictionary and national orthography guidance are available. They do not make my full Tokelauan sentence production defensible; replacing Samoan consonants would be unsafe.

declined.name: Tuvaluan
declined.reason: A specialist TUFS language-and-culture dictionary is available. I cannot reliably compose all technical subordinate clauses and maintain Tuvaluan morphology and orthography.

declined.name: Mongolian (traditional script)
declined.writtenForm: Standard Mongolian in the traditional national script
declined.reason: Real traditional orthography is not a mechanical Cyrillic substitution. I cannot produce the required etymological spellings and contextual forms reliably; rendering also needs suitable shaping/fonts and layout review.

declined.name: Uzbek (Afghanistan, Arabic script)
declined.writtenForm: Southern Uzbek in Afghan Arabic orthography
declined.reason: Afghan Southern Uzbek differs in vocabulary and orthography from Northern Uzbek. I cannot responsibly create this by transliterating the existing Latin Uzbek translation; a Southern Uzbek author and current-status review are needed.

omitted.name: Fiji Hindi
omitted.reason: Fiji Constitution section 3 names Hindi as a constitutional translation language; section 31(3) separately names conversational/contemporary Fiji Hindi for teaching. This evidence does not require a separate colloquial hif website profile. Root confirmed standard hi coverage instead.

omitted.name: Punjabi (Shahmukhi)
omitted.reason: Punjab Assembly Rule 218 permits Punjabi speeches but does not establish general provincewide official status or prescribe Shahmukhi as an official written standard. Root confirmed omission; existing Gurmukhi Punjabi serves Indian official use.

notes: Confidence is a candid authorship assessment, not native-speaker certification. Independent review is still pending.
All repeated English strings share an identical translation within each written file.
Official status of a candidate is not asserted merely because it appears in the declined list; country-level status is tracked separately.
Existing language files outside this assignment, English, catalog, tooling and documentation were not edited.
